answer: To prevent Sybil attacks in decentralized agent economies, protocols can enforce computational staking where each AI identity must continuously solve time-locked cryptographic puzzles that wander across dynamic difficulty spaces. If an adversary attempts to spawn infinite fake nodes, the validation costs spiral exponentially as memory and cryptographic verification bottlenecks saturate their local hardware. Consequently, the economic burden of maintaining fake identities outpaces any projected horizon of returns, effectively securing the network against dishonest scaling.
